implementation_notes: JavaScript mud has a distinct fingerprint: a handful of very large files that re-export everything (`index.js` barrels), and a `require` graph that is not circular but is dense. Circular requires are detectable — `madge --circular` — and in CommonJS they produce the runtime symptom of a half-initialised `module.exports`, which is the tell-tale sign of an architecture problem masquerading as a bug. Consolidation is mostly mechanical: split files by responsibility, have each module import the specific functions it needs rather than the barrel, and let the import graph become the dependency documentation.
idiom_name: one index.js barrel re-exporting everything; circular require graph
pitfalls: A barrel re-export hides the real import edges from tools that only read the barrel, so the graph you measure is not the graph you have.
`npm link`/workspace hoisting can resolve two different copies of the same package and make a shared singleton into two singletons — a mud symptom with a surprising cause.
Bundlers do not enforce import direction, so a cycle stays a cycle until something enforces it.
